_comment: Localization policy, one entry per canonical route that is not already
available in all four locales. This is a REGISTRY, not documentation: the
guards in scripts/tests/route-policy.test.cjs read it, so a route cannot
quietly appear or disappear without a test failing, and a route cannot sit
in limbo without a stated disposition.
LOCALIZE            — should have DE/ES/FR; listed with its word count so
the remaining work is quantified rather than vague.
INTENTIONALLY_EN_ONLY — defensible editorial/market reason for English only.
REDIRECT_OR_OBSOLETE— should not generate locale copies.
'words' is the measured English body word count, so the translation cost of
the backlog is a derived number and not an estimate.

routes.reason: Public product page. eSIMky sells international data plans, so a non-English audience is the core audience, not an edge case. Four sibling products (PDF Editor, Invoice Maker, CV Builder, Pocket Manager) are already localized; this is the same class of page and the asymmetry is an oversight, not a decision.
Public product page in the same family as the already-localized products. Second-number/roaming use cases are strongly international.
Public product page. Fax remains in routine business and administrative use in Germany and France specifically, so the DE/FR versions have clearer value than the English one.
Public product page, same family and same reasoning as the other localized products.
Public product page. Trading-card collecting has large German, French and Spanish markets.
Public product page. A file-archive utility is language-neutral in function, which makes it a low-risk translation with broad reach.
Index of the blog. Thin and structural — mostly card titles and tags — so it should follow whichever posts get localized rather than lead them.
Index page, thin and structural. Same reasoning as /blog/.
Index page, thin and structural — the payload is template names and tags rather than prose, so it should follow the templates it lists rather than lead them.

Substantive evergreen guide tied to an already-localized product. Highest-value long-form candidate, but it carries FAQ structured data whose answers must be translated in step with the visible text — a partial translation would put German prose above English schema answers.
Evergreen explanatory essay with no product or market dependency; translates cleanly.
Evergreen guide tied to an already-listed product page.

Largest single article. Card-collecting terminology is partly untranslatable jargon (set names, grading scales, card conditions) and those are protected tokens, so this one needs a translator who knows the domain rather than a general pass.
Substantive editorial page already linked from the localized footer, so a German reader currently follows a German label to an English page.
Very thin index, linked from the localized footer. Cheap to localize and currently a locale escape.
Very thin index, linked from the localized footer.
Very thin index, linked from the localized footer.

A directory of startups whose own listings, pitches and company names are English. Translating the surrounding chrome would produce a German page whose entire payload is English — the precise failure this programme exists to remove — while implying the listings themselves are available in German.
Live fundraising listings, same reasoning as /startups/. The content is submitted in English by founders and changes continuously; a localized shell around it would misrepresent what a reader gets.
Submission form for the English-language startup directory. The form is processed in English, so a German page inviting a German submission would set an expectation the pipeline does not honour.

_generatedFamiliesComment: EXPLICIT `routes` above are individually maintained exceptions, each with a human-authored reason. `generatedFamilies` below are narrowly scoped route families owned by one generator. The distinction is deliberate: a family is permission for a DEFINED generator to emit routes it can prove correspond to real canonical records, not permission to emit arbitrary paths. A family that could match globally, or that authorized an id with no canonical record behind it, would defeat the registry it lives in. Membership is verified in scripts/lib/route-family.cjs against the generator's own canonical route set.

generatedFamilies.reason: One canonical record per procurement opportunity. The material facts — tender title, buyer, dates, classifications, declared value, source and official URLs — are source facts in the source's own language and are never translated. Four locale copies would be ~531 MB of near-identical files differing only in field labels, so v1 publishes one canonical route and the localized Discovery and Monitoring pages in all four locales link to it. Route identity is the canonical opportunity id, never the English title, so localized shells remain possible later without moving a single URL.
